question.text: What is the maximum Net Overnight Open Position Limit (NOOPL) for banks incorporated in India?

answer.text: 25% of total capital (Tier I and Tier II) or as specified by RBI
50% of total capital (Tier I and Tier II)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 24, NOOP limits are fixed by the Board of each bank but should not exceed 25 per cent of total Tier I and Tier II capital, or such other conditions as specified by RBI. For banks incorporated in India, the limit aggregates all branches including overseas branches and OBUs. The Trap: For foreign banks, the limit covers only their branches in India, not their global branches. Note: The 25 per cent ceiling combines both Tier I and Tier II capital; it is not a Tier I-only or Tier II-only cap.
